<store>
Name: Fernhill Coffee Supply
Sells: Fernhill Coffee Supply sells home coffee brewing equipment and coffee beans. The range covers pour-over gear (ceramic and stainless steel drippers, size 02 paper filters, stovetop and electric gooseneck kettles, and a brew scale with timer), immersion brewers such as a French press and a cold brew jar, and manual and electric burr grinders. It also sells single-origin coffee beans from Fernhill Roastery in 250 g and 1 kg bags, whole bean or ground.
Audience: People who brew coffee at home, especially by pour-over or immersion, and who want to grind, weigh and control water temperature themselves. Some products, such as the single-dose flat-burr grinder and the temperature-hold kettle, suit buyers who care about precise brewing.
Tone: expert
Never say: —
</store>

content.text: {"title":"How to Use a French Press: A Step-by-Step Guide to a Clean, Full-Bodied Cup","angle":"The reader will know the full French press method (ratio, grind, water, steep, plunge, pour), why each step matters for a clean yet full-bodied cup, and which grinder and beans make it easy to repeat.","sections":[{"heading":"Why the French Press Makes Such a Full-Bodied Cup","covers":"How immersion brewing works: grounds steep fully in water, then a metal mesh separates them, letting oils and fine particles through for body. Introduces the Fernhill French Press and its construction.","facts":["F2","F4","F5","F7"]},{"heading":"What You Need: Ratio, Water and Batch Size","covers":"General starting ratio (around 1:15–1:16, e.g. 60 g coffee to 1 litre water), water just off the boil (about 93–96 °C), a scale and timer. How to scale the recipe to a 1 litre press that makes about 4 mugs.","facts":["F1","F6"]},{"heading":"Get the Grind Right: Coarse and Even","covers":"Why French press needs a coarse, uniform grind; too fine causes sludge and bitterness, too coarse tastes thin. Grinding fresh just before brewing with a burr grinder that has a dedicated coarse range, and grinding in batches when the hopper capacity is smaller than a full-press dose.","facts":["F10","F12","F13","F14","F15"]},{"heading":"Step by Step: Bloom, Steep, Break the Crust, Plunge","covers":"Preheat the beaker, add grounds, pour all water, stir gently, steep 4 minutes, break and skim the crust and foam, optionally wait a few more minutes for fines to settle, then press slowly and only to just above the grounds.","facts":["F7"]},{"heading":"Pour Immediately for a Cleaner Cup","covers":"Decant all coffee right away so it stops extracting; leave the last sludgy portion in the beaker. Tips for adjusting taste: bitter means coarser or shorter, sour or thin means finer or longer.","facts":[]},{"heading":"Choosing Beans for French Press","covers":"Medium roasts with chocolate and caramel sweetness shine with the press's body; a fruity natural is an option for a more vivid cup. Buy whole bean and grind fresh.","facts":["F19","F28","F30","F22","F40","F41"]},{"heading":"Cleaning and Care","covers":"Discard grounds (not down the sink), disassemble the plunger and mesh regularly to remove trapped oils that turn rancid, and what to do if the glass breaks.","facts":["F8","F9"]}],"products":["P1","P2","P3","P4"],"links":["P1","P2","P3","P4","L1","L2","L3"]}
